canonical_statement_en: Confirmed: The eight primary screens named in §16.1.1 must exist. Illustrative titles, navigation labels, data values, and repeated dashboard panels are retained separately from confirmed functional contracts. The sample figures do not establish complete forms or API response schemas.
SF-SCP-001: Create enterprise knowledge cases, supply business context and attachments, classify cases, and correct classification labels with a reason code.
SF-SCP-002: Search permitted evidence, inspect immutable source versions and anchors, request grounded AI drafts, and examine execution progress and policy checkpoints.
SF-SCP-003: Route uncertain, sensitive, and high-impact recommendations to authorized human reviewers. Publish only when required evidence and approval policy are satisfied.
SF-SCP-004: Edit authorized case metadata, execute explicit case-state transitions, and close cases while preserving approved-output lineage. Reopening requires a new revision.
SF-SCP-005: Manage connectors and workspace policy, inspect synchronization health, and obtain immutable audit evidence subject to access and redaction scope.

SF-SCP-006: Support manual case editing and evidence search during generation outages. Lexical retrieval may continue during vector-index degradation with a visible reduced-quality flag. Authorization and approval controls remain enforced.

Physical automation and irreversible financial transactions: The platform processes enterprise knowledge and user-submitted cases, not these activities. Financial-impact categories may still be policy inputs.
Foundation-model fine-tuning: Explicitly excluded from the platform.
Unrestricted browsing and administrative cloud permissions for agents: Explicitly excluded; the browser must not submit arbitrary tool definitions.
Application-hosted GPU inference: Providers are external dependencies; GPU inference is not hosted within the application.
Cross-region active/active mutation, OCR beyond English, and customer-managed model weights: The source explicitly defers these capabilities. English OCR fallback remains opt-in.
Secrets and internal model prompts in tenant export: Explicitly excluded from the export package.
Analyst: Opens cases, evaluates evidence, creates attachments, and requests AI runs. Can read authorized case revisions, run details, and run streams.
Analyst: Cannot approve their own high-risk recommendation. Case mutation uses the separate Owner scope in Appendix A.2. Whether all Analysts may edit all workspace cases is not established. OQ-003.
Reviewer: Approves or rejects recommendations
Reviewer: reads authorized cases, run details, and run streams
Reviewer: inspects exact candidate content, citations, model/prompt version, and policy reasons.

Reviewer: Selection depends on policy, organizational role, reviewer pools, minimum role, and separation of duties. Assignment-specific viewing rights and complete action guards need confirmation. OQ-003, OQ-013.
Workspace Admin / Admin
Workspace Admin / Admin: Manages connectors and policy. The API catalog grants Admin connector sync, usage access, and evaluation creation.
Auditor: Obtains immutable evidence without editing case content
Auditor: sees decision metadata, prompt-template digests, and access events within redacted scope. Reads cursor-paginated immutable audit events.
Service: Baseline noninteractive role used for scoped service operations.
Service: No interactive screen access is confirmed.
Owner: Scope for PATCH /v1/cases/{caseId}.
Member: Scope for POST /v1/search.
Member: Not listed as a baseline role. Eligible role combinations and workspace-membership requirements need confirmation. OQ-003.
approver / elevated override actor
approver / elevated override actor: Export and deletion require Admin + approver
approver / elevated override actor: an override requires elevated role, secondary reviewer, and audited reason.

SF-AUTH-001 — Confirmed: Screen visibility is not an authorization boundary. Each operation must evaluate role, tenant, workspace membership, case sensitivity, originating document ACL, action, and segregation-of-duties constraints. Domain services re-evaluate resource attributes within the transaction.
SF-AUTH-002 — Confirmed: Foreign-tenant ID substitution must return the same class of not-found response as an absent ID. Denials must not reveal private resource existence.

SF-PRE-001: Interactive authentication uses OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE. Tokens contain issuer, audience, expiry, subject, and tenant. Unexpected algorithms or missing tenancy claims are rejected.
SF-PRE-002: The browser must not store long-lived refresh tokens in local storage. A backend-for-frontend can issue secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies
SF-PRE-002: this is not a mandatory selected architecture.
SF-PRE-003: Every request is authenticated and tenant-bound; resource access must satisfy workspace and resource authorization.
SF-PRE-004: Incomplete provisioning is visible and blocks connector sync. Provisioning establishes workspace policy, encryption references, role bindings, quotas, and connector stubs.
SF-PRE-005: Evidence must have current permission and resolvable source anchors before it can support generation or citation display.
SF-PRE-006: Durable mutations carry tenant, revision, actor, occurrence time, and correlation context. Trusted identity and tenancy must not be editable user inputs.
SF-PRE-007: New AI runs require admissible workspace tokens, queue age, and provider capacity. Throttling returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After
SF-PRE-007: saved cases remain available.

SF-GEN-001: Use accessible text for AI artifact labels DRAFT, NEEDS_REVIEW, and PUBLISHED. Color or styling must not substitute for text. These are not additional Case status values.
SF-GEN-002: Target WCAG 2.2 AA behavior, visible focus, semantic regions, and robust keyboard ordering. Live updates announce only meaningful state transitions.
SF-GEN-003: Server timestamps remain UTC/RFC 3339. Display workspace-local times with timezone labels. Locale changes presentation, not event ordering or durable API representations.
SF-GEN-004: Never show partial processing as an approved answer or publish an unapproved high-risk response.

SF-GEN-005: Validate state-changing requests before allocating work. If a dependency is unavailable, return a documented retryable error or persisted asynchronous job identifier, never ambiguous success.
SF-GEN-006: Distinguish accepted asynchronous work from completed work. Attachment upload, AI-run creation, connector sync, evaluation creation, export, and deletion return HTTP 202 where cataloged.
SF-GEN-007: Use revision preconditions for case changes. A conflict returns HTTP 409, CASE_VERSION_CONFLICT, and current revision information.
SF-GEN-008: Job-creating POST mutations require Idempotency-Key. Identical repeated requests return the original outcome
SF-GEN-008: changed fingerprints under the same key return IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Case keys bind actor and request fingerprint for 24 hours.
SF-GEN-009: Rejected stale or unauthorized mutations leave business state unchanged. Accepted transitions have one accepted business outcome and correlated audit evidence under replay.

SF-GEN-010: Do not expose secrets, raw provider credentials, full prompts, retrieved documents in errors, or unauthorized resource existence. Diagnostic telemetry must not contain source document text or API secrets.

SF-GEN-011: Retrieved documents and model responses are untrusted data. They cannot authorize tools, change tenant scope, modify approvals, or bypass the deterministic policy engine. The browser never submits arbitrary tool definitions.

API-SCP-001 — Confirmed: External interfaces use REST. Internal HTTP and gRPC contracts are versioned, generated, and independently authorized. OpenAPI governs REST clients
protobuf IDL governs internal gRPC messages.

API-SCP-002 — Confirmed: The browser enters through the edge API. The orchestrator has no direct database credentials and uses narrow scoped interfaces. Internal endpoints in this specification are not automatically browser-accessible.

API-SCP-003 — Confirmed: The API layer must preserve permitted evidence, immutable source versions, deterministic approval gates, tenant isolation, and idempotent cross-service writes. Untrusted evidence or model responses cannot authorize tools, alter tenant scope, change approvals, or bypass policy.
These profiles apply to every inventory entry that references them.
I — Interactive/public API

I — Interactive/public API: Authenticated principal and tenant. OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE for interactive sessions. Access tokens carry issuer, audience, expiry, subject, and tenant. Reject unexpected algorithms and missing tenancy claims. Evaluate resource authorization independently of screen visibility.
S — Internal service API

S — Internal service API: TLS; mTLS-authenticated HTTP or gRPC for internal calls; service audience checks; scoped IAM/service credentials; independently authorized resource and tenant access. Prefer managed workload identity where supported; do not share service identity between deployment units.
O — Operational interface

O — Operational interface: Apply authenticated, scoped operational/service access. The source does not establish anonymous access merely because an endpoint is used for health, metrics, capacity, replay, or release operations.
T — Tool/agent interface

T — Tool/agent interface: Scoped service credentials and separate capability authorization. Invocation depends on principal, workspace policy, tool scope, and data classification. Discovery is not permission.
W — Optional outbound webhook
W — Optional outbound webhook: Signed delivery; recipient verifies signature and event age. Failure cannot roll back the case transition.

API-AUTH-001 — Confirmed: Resource access combines role, tenant, workspace membership, case sensitivity, originating document ACL, requested action, and segregation-of-duties constraints. Domain services re-evaluate resource attributes within the transaction.

API-AUTH-002 — Confirmed: A foreign-tenant identifier returns the same class of not-found response as an absent identifier. Denials retain the principal and denied resource class in audit evidence without revealing private resource existence.
API-AUTH-003 — Confirmed: Tenant identity participates in every storage predicate. Tenant-owned rows use tenant-scoped database context and RLS

background jobs carry immutable tenant identity in signed envelopes. Connection-pool scoped session variables must reset after every transaction. Workspace-tenancy membership must be enforced by foreign keys or controlled write procedures.
API-AUTH-004 — Confirmed: The browser does not store long-lived refresh tokens in local storage. A BFF *can* issue secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies
that architecture is not selected by the source. Credentials must not appear in traces or model prompts.

it does not establish an undocumented success status or asynchronous fallback schema.

API-CLS-001 — Confirmed: Maximum included-material classification

Data classes are PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, and RESTRICTED. For every run, the model route, log redaction, retention, and approval policy depend on the maximum class of any material included in that run.
Model route: Select and constrain initial/fallback deployment using the highest included-material class, not only the case sensitivity
Log redaction: Apply the redaction policy associated with the highest included-material class
Log redaction: global prohibitions on document/secret diagnostics still apply
Retention: Apply retention policy based on that highest class, preserving legal holds and immutable approved lineage
Approval policy: Use the highest included-material class when determining approval requirements and validating publication
An INTERNAL case that includes permitted RESTRICTED evidence must invoke RESTRICTED controls for all four categories.
Source ACL permission is necessary but not sufficient to select a lower model route or approval requirement.
Under the reference configuration, require_human_review_for: [HIGH_RISK, RESTRICTED] applies. HIGH_RISK is a risk category, not an additional information class.
auto_publish_classification: INTERNAL is not permission to auto-publish a run that includes RESTRICTED material or otherwise fails evidence/risk/approval gates.
The stored case’s lower sensitivity must not be treated as the complete run-control classification. The source does not require automatically rewriting the case sensitivity to implement this rule.

No additional public response property, client-controlled classification value, or seventh policy input is established. The rule is a shared control obligation across the existing run, model, policy, diagnostic, retention, and publication boundaries.
Additional source: S, p. 90, Appendix F; pp. 37–39, Chapter 10; pp. 44–46, Chapter 12.

Permission failures are permanent and not automatically retried. Use ERR-035 and 429 plus Retry-After for failed new-run token, queue-age, or provider-capacity admission checks.
